learningObjective: Understand FlashAttention's tiling + online softmax + IO-aware fusion; distinguish exact algorithm from approximation.

canonicalClaims.claim: FlashAttention tiles Q, K, V and processes K/V tiles for a fixed Q tile while maintaining a running (m, l, acc) via the online-softmax recurrence. This eliminates materialization of the O(S^2) score matrix in HBM and reduces HBM traffic to O(S) for long sequences, while remaining an exact algorithm (bit-different from naive due to summation order only).
conditions: SMEM large enough for tiled Q/K/V blocks.
Standard forward pass (backward has its own recurrence).
nonImplications: Does not imply speedup for very small S.
Does not imply v1, v2, v3 are identical implementations.

misconceptions.whyWrong: It is exact algebra; differs from naive only by summation order (rounding).

misconceptions.claim: FlashAttention replaces exp with a cheaper approximation.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It uses standard exp; the speedup comes from IO-awareness and tiling.

misconceptions.claim: The `acc` rescale is optional if we accept minor precision loss.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It is required for correctness — without it, `acc` mixes different anchors and gives wrong results.

misconceptions.claim: FlashAttention has the same HBM traffic as naive attention.
misconceptions.whyWrong: HBM traffic drops from O(S^2) to O(S) per (batch, head) — the central contribution.

implementationFacts: V2 improves work partitioning and eliminates non-matmul stalls.
V3 targets Hopper with warp-specialization and TMA.
performanceScenarios: FlashAttention's kernel-level speedups over naive on long-context depend on hardware (A100/H100), shape, and precision; paper-reported numbers are Kernel-level, not always end-to-end 1:1.
